title: Thin Codex wrapper patterns around skills and MCP
key_findings: A common Codex plugin pattern is a thin wrapper: keep runtime wiring small, put guidance in skills, and keep plugin metadata explicit.
The example plugin keeps its MCP wiring in .mcp.json and uses the manifest to describe install behavior and discovery metadata.
Community examples emphasize staying close to upstream tools instead of forking or re-implementing them inside the plugin.
recommended_actions: Port the existing skill-bearing plugins first instead of trying to re-create every Claude-specific surface in Codex.
Leave unsupported host-specific behavior out of the Codex manifests unless the repo actually bundles the needed Codex surface.
Use README notes to explain the thin-wrapper boundary and any host-specific limitations.
